---
title: "simulated_ovarian_cancer_diagnosis_prediction"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Simulated ovarian cancer dataset (for re-doing BOTH files later)
# Only DATA SIMULATION for now
# ============================================================

set.seed(20260224)

n <- 1200  # sample size

# -----------------------
# 1) Patient baseline covariates
# -----------------------
age <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 58, sd = 12))
age <- pmin(pmax(age, 18), 90)

postmenopausal <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis((age - 50) / 4))  # increases with age
family_history <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.18)

brca <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(family_history == 1, 0.22, 0.08))  # enriched among FH+
bmi  <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 26, sd = 4), 1)
bmi  <- pmin(pmax(bmi, 16), 45)

# Symptoms / clinical context
symptom_score <- pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n, mean = 1.1 + 0.35*postmenopausal, sd = 0.9), 0), 0), 3) # 0..3

# Ultrasound morphology score (e.g., IOTA-like ordinal)
us_score <- sample(0:3, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.28, 0.20, 0.12)) # 0..3

# Imaging / clinical findings
ascites <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-2.2 + 0.6*us_score + 0.3*symptom_score))

# -----------------------
# 2) Latent "malignancy risk" to induce realistic correlation structure
# -----------------------
# This latent factor will drive biomarkers + tumor size + true cancer status
latent_risk <- 0.03*(age - 58) +
               0.9*brca +
               0.55*us_score +
               0.35*symptom_score +
               0.65*ascites +
               rnorm(n, 0, 1)

# -----------------------
# 3) Biomarkers (right-skewed; use log-scale internally)
# -----------------------
# CA-125 (U/mL) and HE4 (pmol/L), plus CEA for realism (less specific)
log_ca125 <- 4.1 + 0.60*latent_risk + rnorm(n, 0, 0.60)
log_he4   <- 3.55 + 0.50*latent_risk + rnorm(n, 0, 0.50)
log_cea   <- 1.5 + 0.15*latent_risk + rnorm(n, 0, 0.45)

ca125 <- exp(log_ca125)
he4   <- exp(log_he4)
cea   <- exp(log_cea)

# Optional: ROMA-like score (not exactly ROMA formula, just a correlated marker)
roma_proxy <- plogis(-3.0 + 0.015*age + 0.8*postmenopausal + 0.9*log(ca125) + 0.8*log(he4))

# -----------------------
# 4) True ovarian cancer status (binary outcome)
# -----------------------
# Generate event probability from a "truth" model (not equal to any later fitted model)
linpred_true <- -7.2 +
                0.035*age +
                1.10*brca +
                0.70*us_score +
                0.40*symptom_score +
                0.85*ascites +
                1.05*log(ca125) +
                0.85*log(he4)

p_true <- plogis(linpred_true)
ovarian_cancer <- rbinom(n, 1, p_true)

# -----------------------
# 5) Continuous measurement for agreement tasks (File 1)
#    e.g., tumor maximal diameter (mm) and a "risk score" (0-100)
# -----------------------
tumor_diam_true <- pmax(0, rnorm(n, mean = 18 + 28*ovarian_cancer + 6*us_score + 5*ascites, sd = 12))

risk_score_true <- pmin(pmax(round(100*plogis(-2.5 + 0.9*latent_risk + 0.25*ovarian_cancer) + rnorm(n, 0, 3)), 0), 100)

# -----------------------
# 6) Two raters / readers (for Kappa + ICC + CCC)
# -----------------------
# Binary classification by two clinicians: "malignant?" (for Cohen's kappa)
# Use noisy versions of a latent diagnostic signal and different thresholds
diag_signal_A <- scale(linpred_true + rnorm(n, 0, 1.0))[,1]
diag_signal_B <- scale(linpred_true + rnorm(n, 0, 1.0))[,1]

raterA_malignant <- ifelse(diag_signal_A > 0.00, 1, 0)
raterB_malignant <- ifelse(diag_signal_B > 0.15, 1, 0)  # slightly more conservative

# Continuous measurement by two radiologists: tumor diameter with noise + slight bias
raterA_diam <- tumor_diam_true + rnorm(n, 0, 4.0)
raterB_diam <- tumor_diam_true + 2.5 + rnorm(n, 0, 4.5)  # systematic +2.5mm bias

# Another continuous score (for CCC demonstration)
raterA_risk <- pmin(pmax(risk_score_true + rnorm(n, 0, 6), 0), 100)
raterB_risk <- pmin(pmax(risk_score_true + 5 + rnorm(n, 0, 7), 0), 100) # systematic +5 bias

# -----------------------
# 7) Assemble final dataset
# -----------------------
ovca_dat <- data.frame(
  ovarian_cancer = ovarian_cancer,
  age = age,
  postmenopausal = postmenopausal,
  bmi = bmi,
  family_history = family_history,
  brca = brca,
  symptom_score = symptom_score,
  us_score = us_score,
  ascites = ascites,
  ca125 = ca125,
  he4 = he4,
  cea = cea,
  roma_proxy = roma_proxy,
  tumor_diam_true = tumor_diam_true,
  risk_score_true = risk_score_true,
  raterA_malignant = raterA_malignant,
  raterB_malignant = raterB_malignant,
  raterA_diam = raterA_diam,
  raterB_diam = raterB_diam,
  raterA_risk = raterA_risk,
  raterB_risk = raterB_risk
)

# Quick sanity checks (optional prints)
cat("n =", n, "\n")
cat("Simulated ovarian cancer prevalence =", round(mean(ovca_dat$ovarian_cancer), 3), "\n")
summary(ovca_dat[, c("age","ca125","he4","us_score","ascites","ovarian_cancer")])


names(ovca_dat)
```
# What is the level of agreement between two clinicians in classifying ovarian tumors as malignant vs benign?

```{r}

table_AB <- table(
  ovca_dat$raterA_malignant,
  ovca_dat$raterB_malignant
)

table_AB
```
```{r}
observed_agreement <- sum(diag(table_AB)) / sum(table_AB)
observed_agreement

#The two raters agreed in 85% of cases.
```
```{r}
install.packages("psych")   # only once
library(psych)

kappa_result <- cohen.kappa(table_AB)
kappa_result

# There is substantial agreement between the two raters in classifying ovarian tumors as malignant vs benign (κ = 0.66, 95% CI 0.61–0.70).


```
# How reliable are tumor diameter measurements between the two radiologists?


```{r}
library(psych)

diam_data <- ovca_dat[, c("raterA_diam", "raterB_diam")]

icc_result <- ICC(diam_data)
icc_result


# The tumor diameter measurements demonstrate excellent absolute agreement between the two raters (ICC = 0.923).

```
```{r}

model2 <- glm(
  ovarian_cancer ~ age +
    log(ca125) +
    log(he4) +
    brca +
    us_score +
    ascites,
  data = ovca_dat,
  family = binomial()
)

p <- predict(model2, type = "response")

library(pROC)
roc_obj <- roc(ovca_dat$ovarian_cancer, p)

auc(roc_obj)
ci.auc(roc_obj)

```
